docusaurus_conventions.overview: This guide covers Docusaurus-specific formatting rules for Roo Code documentation. Before applying these conventions, always explore the project structure to understand the actual directory layout.

discovery_first.principle: Always use list_files to discover the actual project structure before making assumptions about paths
Check for existing patterns in similar files before creating new content
Verify directory existence before referencing specific paths

rule.name: internal_links
rule.description: Use paths relative to the documentation root. Do not include the `.md` extension. Discover the documentation structure first.

discovery_steps.step: Use list_files to find the documentation root directory
Identify the path structure used in existing documentation

rule.name: site_alias
rule.description: Use `@site` for code imports or asset references from the project root. Do not use it for Markdown links.

rule.name: images
rule.description: Discover the image storage location in the project before placing images. Look for existing image references to understand the pattern.

discovery_steps.step: Use list_files to find where images are stored (commonly in static/img or similar)
Check existing documentation for image reference patterns

rule.name: no_version_numbers
rule.description: Do not include version numbers or phrases like "as of version X.Y" in general documentation. First discover where version information is stored in the project.

discovery_steps.step: Use list_files to find version-related documentation directories
Check for patterns like update-notes, changelog, or release directories
Place version-specific information in the appropriate location

rule.name: metadata
rule.description: Check existing documentation files for frontmatter patterns before adding new ones. The required fields may vary by project.

discovery_steps.step: Read several existing documentation files to understand the frontmatter pattern
Identify which fields are consistently used

rule.example: --- description: A concise summary of the page content. keywords: - relevant - keywords - for - search image: /img/social-share.jpg ---

general_discovery_workflow.step: Use list_files to explore the project structure
Read existing files similar to what you're creating/editing
Identify patterns in paths, formatting, and conventions
Follow the established patterns rather than assuming standard locations
When in doubt, ask for clarification rather than making assumptions

redundancy_prevention_workflow.overview: Before making any documentation changes, follow this workflow to prevent redundancy and ensure cohesion.

step.title: Content Discovery

actions.action: Use codebase_search to find all mentions of the topic or feature
Search for variations of key terms (e.g., "configuration", "config", "setup")
Note all locations where related information exists

step.example: <!-- Search for existing content about a feature --> <codebase_search> <query>authentication setup configuration</query> <path>docs</path> </codebase_search>

actions.action: Read all discovered related content thoroughly
Identify if the requested change would duplicate existing information
Determine if consolidation is needed instead of addition

scenario.action: Inform user and suggest updating existing location
Enhance existing content rather than creating new

scenario.condition: Content is scattered across multiple files
scenario.action: Consider consolidation into a single authoritative location

actions.action: Check all internal links that might be affected
Verify that moving or changing content won't break existing references
Update docusaurus.config.ts redirects if moving content
Ensure consistent use of technical terms across all documentation
Check glossary or terminology guide if one exists
Maintain consistent naming for features, tools, and concepts

guideline.name: information_architecture
guideline.description: Maintain logical information hierarchy and flow

checks.check: Does this content belong in the current section?
Would users expect to find this information here?
Does it follow the progression from basic to advanced?

guideline.name: single_source_of_truth
guideline.description: Each piece of information should have one authoritative location

implementation.step: Core information lives in one place
Other locations reference the authoritative source
Use includes or references rather than duplication

guideline.name: contextual_linking
guideline.description: Connect related content through meaningful links

best_practices.practice: Link to prerequisites before advanced topics
Provide "See also" sections for related content

documentation_update_protocol.overview: When updating existing documentation, follow this protocol to maintain quality and prevent issues.

pre_update_validation.step: Identify all documents that reference the content being updated
Check for dependent examples or tutorials that might need updating
Verify that the update won't invalidate existing instructions
Consider backward compatibility if documenting changed features

update_impact_assessment.question: Will this update require changes to other documents?
Are there code examples that need to be updated?
Do any quickstart guides or tutorials reference this content?
Will this change affect the logical flow of the documentation?

post_update_checklist.item: No broken links have been introduced
Terminology remains consistent across all affected documents
The update enhances rather than contradicts existing content

ask_before_proceeding.description: Use ask_followup_question when uncertainty exists about redundancy or impact

scenarios.scenario: When similar content exists in multiple locations
When the requested change might contradict existing documentation
When consolidation might be better than addition
When the impact on other documents is unclear

ask_before_proceeding.example: <ask_followup_question> <question>I found existing content about this topic in three different locations. How would you like me to proceed?</question> <follow_up> <suggest>Update the main guide and add cross-references from the other locations</suggest> <suggest>Consolidate all information into a single comprehensive guide</suggest> <suggest>Keep them separate but ensure they're consistent and cross-linked</suggest> <suggest>Show me the existing locations first so I can decide</suggest> </follow_up> </ask_followup_question>
